# The SlashForge Spec Home

Every repo SlashForge manages keeps its living specs as Markdown under
`docs/slashforge/`. This is the source of truth the workflow reads and writes —
not the dated HTML reports, which are point-in-time artefacts. Specs are
Markdown on purpose: they must diff cleanly, grep, and review in a pull request.

```
docs/slashforge/
├─ constitution.md          # non-negotiables (human-authored; rules reference it)
├─ architecture.md          # tech stack, standards, design patterns
├─ status.md                # what is active now + recently archived
├─ active/                  # changes currently being built
│  └─ <change-slug>/
│     ├─ requirements.md     # WHAT & WHY (product scope)
│     ├─ plan.md             # HOW (files changed, schemas, approach)
│     └─ tasks.md            # sequential checklist, - [ ] / - [x]
└─ archive/                 # completed changes, moved here unchanged on merge
   └─ <change-slug>/
```

The change slug is a short kebab name chosen at intake (e.g. `oauth-login`). If
`active/` or `archive/` already holds that slug, append `-2`, `-3`, … rather than
overwrite.

## The three top-level documents

- **`constitution.md`** — the project's non-negotiables: architectural rules,
  quality bars, things that must never happen. Human-authored and rarely changed.
  The project's generated rule files **reference** this file as the source of
  non-negotiables rather than restating them, so there is one source and no drift.
- **`architecture.md`** — the tech stack, the build/test/lint commands, the design
  patterns and conventions a contributor needs. Generated by setup from codebase
  exploration and refreshed as the system grows.
- **`status.md`** — a short index of what is in `active/` right now and what was
  most recently archived (with merge dates). The one file to read to learn where
  the project stands.

## File formats

Each is plain Markdown. Keep headings exactly as below so the workflow and a human
reader find the same sections.

### `requirements.md` — WHAT & WHY

```markdown
# <Change> — Requirements

## Goal
One sentence: what this change achieves.

## Problem
What is wrong or missing today, and why it matters.

## Behaviour
What the user can do once this ships.

## Constraints & out of scope
- ...

## Success criteria
- A checkable statement proving the change is done.
```

### `plan.md` — HOW

```markdown
# <Change> — Plan

## Approach
2–3 sentences on the shape of the change.

## Files
- Create / Modify / Remove — exact paths and the responsibility of each.

## Risks & edge cases
- ...

## Test strategy
What will be tested and how it is proven.
```

### `tasks.md` — the checklist

```markdown
# <Change> — Tasks

## Task 1: <name>
- [ ] Step 1: write the failing test
- [ ] Step 2: run it, confirm it FAILS
- [ ] Step 3: minimal implementation
- [ ] Step 4: run it, confirm it PASSES
- [ ] Step 5: commit
```

Flip `- [ ]` to `- [x]` in place as each step completes — `tasks.md` is a live
document, not a record written once.

## The lifecycle

The phases of `/slashforge-code` are the lifecycle; there are no separate
commands.

| Stage | Phase | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| Propose  | 1 (brainstorm) | write `active/<change>/requirements.md` |
| Plan     | 2 (plan)       | write `active/<change>/plan.md` + `tasks.md` |
| Apply    | 5 (implement)  | work `tasks.md`, flipping `- [ ]` to `- [x]` |
| Converge | 6 (verify)     | check every success criterion in `requirements.md`; all task boxes ticked |
| Review   | 7 (review)     | change matches `requirements.md` and honours `constitution.md` |
| Archive  | 10 (post-merge)| move `active/<change>/` → `archive/<change>/`; update `status.md` |

The lean path (`/slashforge-code -quick`) writes a lean `plan.md` + `tasks.md` and
skips `requirements.md`. A trivial change that never created an `active/<change>/`
folder has nothing to archive — skip the move silently.
